key_insight: The paper shows that LVLMs can be made more reliable for visual reasoning by training them to give consistent answers to logically equivalent questions, not just correct ones.
engineering_relevance: For dependable multimodal systems, consistency constraints provide a practical way to improve robustness in complex visual reasoning tasks where single-answer accuracy is not enough.
method: Built ConVBench: a vision-centric benchmark with paired logically equivalent questions across six reasoning categories.
Defined two metrics: logical consistency and robust accuracy to evaluate both agreement and correctness.
Trained ConVLM with GRPO reinforcement learning using a dual reward for accuracy and consistency, with automatically generated paired QA data.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a benchmark of images paired with two logically equivalent questions across six categories and evaluates models with both logical consistency and robust accuracy.
watch_item: Automatically generated equivalent-question pairs may introduce noise or bias, so the quality of pair generation and reward design is important for stable training.
paper_title: Be Consistent! Enhancing Robust Visual Reasoning in LVLMs with Consistency Constraints
